symptom: `check --references` passed drop/rename/move of a document that does not exist, and alter enumeration / alter microflow on one, while exec refused each with `<kind> not found` — 9 of the 11 statement forms that name an existing document (only alter entity and alter page were resolved)
cause: validateAlterTarget was written for ALTER and extended one statement at a time; the drop/rename/move statements resolve against the same listings but were never routed to it
file: mdl/executor/validate_alter_target.go (validateAlterTarget, targetListing, checkTarget, moveTargetKind), mdl/executor/validate.go (collectSingle: indirectDocs, renamedModules, opaqueModules, opaqueScript); test cmd/mxcli/check_statement_target_test.go
insight: The risk in widening a not-found check is the false refusal, not the miss: a document can reach a name without a create statement naming it — an earlier rename or move, a rename module, an execute script, a generated SQL connector, a business event service, a bulk external-entities import. Record each in the pre-pass and stay silent for that name or module; the check must stay quieter than exec. Matching is exact-case because exec's lookups are. A PedApp test per form, each with an existing-target control, plus if-exists / created / renamed / moved controls. Control: without the new cases all 13 forms pass check.
